global.headline: THE MISSILE WARNING IS BACK ON AFTER OSLO, AND ZELENSKY OFFERS A REFINERY TRUCE FOR PATRIOTS
summary: Zelensky said after meeting Steve Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday that the United States has resumed advance warning of Russian ballistic launches: "Now it works. It's great." Jared Kushner joined by video, alongside Norwegian, Finnish, EU and British officials. He said he had offered to halt Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries — Trump's central demand — if Washington releases Patriot interceptors, which the Pentagon has blocked even when allies pay, and that he raised the Starshield slowdown with Marco Rubio.

He rejected a Putin-floated Trump–Putin–Xi summit next month that would exclude Kyiv: "There can be nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine." Kaja Kallas questioned whether US negotiators had been honest brokers; Rubio, in India, denied any directive to harm Ukraine and said interceptors are simply scarce. Nine people were killed in Ukraine on Tuesday.
global.geopolitical: The feed went off and back on inside a week, and the price list is now visible: a refinery truce for interceptors. A capability Kyiv cannot replace is now a bargaining chip.
global.socioeconomic: Ukraine's refinery strikes are one of the two causes the IEA blames for diesel at double its pre-war price, so the trade Zelensky offered to save his cities is also the quickest route to cheaper fuel everywhere.

global.headline: NATO SENDS AIRCRAFT AND RADARS TO THE BLACK SEA AS FIVE MORE CARGO SHIPS ARE HIT
summary: NATO ambassadors met in the North Atlantic Council on Tuesday and agreed to send maritime patrol aircraft, radar, drones and intelligence personnel to the Black Sea for "surveillance, reconnaissance, and forensics". Russia's military said the same day it had struck three cargo vessels in Ukraine's port of Reni and two more bound for Odesa. At least five cargo ships have been hit off Romania and Bulgaria in a fortnight, 23 sailors dead or missing, mostly outside NATO territorial waters; the London market's new high-risk designation now covers the whole sea except Romanian, Bulgarian and Turkish waters.

Romania has logged 35 unauthorised drone incursions this year against nine in all of 2025, and downed two at the weekend — Geran-4 turboprop drones flying at 450kmh, defence minister Radu Miruță said; Bulgaria has asked NATO for combat aircraft. The risk analyst Ambrey attributes about 80 per cent of the attacks to Russian forces, and the death toll to "double tap" strikes pairing aerial with surface drones carrying up to half a tonne of explosives.
global.geopolitical: NATO is buying evidence rather than air defence: forensics commit it to proving who fired, not to firing back, so the alliance's likeliest accident — a member's jet against a Russian drone — is untouched.
global.socioeconomic: Insurance, not ordnance, is doing the blockading: with the whole sea bar three coastal strips rated high-risk, Ukraine's grain and the Danube barge trade are priced out of their own export route.

global.headline: BRENT HOLDS ABOVE US$111 AS THE IEA SAYS 2027 WILL NOT BE NORMAL, AND BRITAIN REARRESTS TWO OVER FAIRFORD
summary: "I don't see any credible pathway that 2027 will be a year of normalisation," IEA executive director Fatih Birol told a London summit on Tuesday; Hormuz has been closed once and "it can be closed again". Brent traded above US$111, on course for its highest settlement since May. Birol called judging the crisis by crude "myopic": diesel has doubled from pre-war levels as refinery maintenance season starts, and "we are on thin ice". Its members hold 1.6 billion barrels after March's record 400-million-barrel release. Middle East outflows are just above the pre-war average at 24 million barrels a day, restored Saudi pipeline exports offsetting the strait.

British counter-terrorism police rearrested a 24-year-old Briton and a 25-year-old dual British-Iranian under Section 3 of the National Security Act — assisting a foreign intelligence service — over last month's RAF Fairford plot. Seven men have now been arrested, five on bail; "we consider it highly likely that there is Iranian state involvement", said Laurence Taylor; the US bombers withdrawn from the base have not returned. Pete Hegseth paid an unannounced visit to Israel to see Netanyahu and his defence minister, a week before the election.
global.geopolitical: Iran no longer has to close the strait to collect on it — the option is priced into every barrel — and the Fairford charges put Tehran's reach inside a NATO country onto a British charge sheet.
global.socioeconomic: Doubled diesel is the figure that reaches households, setting freight, farming and food costs; Washington answered the same day with an US$8 billion farm relief package aimed at fuel and fertiliser bills.

global.headline: RAF TYPHOONS WILL FLY OVER SAUDI CITIES, AND THE TOLL AT THE YEMENI TRAINING CAMP REACHES 73
summary: Britain will send Typhoons to fly defensive missions over Saudi cities and critical infrastructure, shooting down Houthi missiles and drones — the largest military commitment of Andy Burnham's premiership. The Ministry of Defence did not say how many aircraft and insisted they "will not conduct offensive strikes"; an A400M transport is being added and the Voyager refuelling mission extended by 90 days. Defence secretary Wes Streeting said the UK was "responding to protect civilians"; the deployment was justified partly by what Middle East instability is doing to energy prices.

The toll from Monday's missile strike on a government training camp in Shabwa rose to 73. Nineteen people have been killed in Saudi Arabia since September, 13 of them at Riyadh's King Khalid airport. The Houthis have cut the roads into Taiz, besieging one of Yemen's largest cities, whose officials warn of humanitarian disaster. Washington has sent more than 100 military advisers and intelligence support but no combat forces, and Trump urged Riyadh on Friday to accept Israeli help.
global.geopolitical: A second Western air force enters the Gulf war on an undefined word. As RUSI's HA Hellyer asked: "What does defensive mean?" if a Houthi boat attacks a Saudi ship and a Typhoon is in range.
global.socioeconomic: Britain is spending militarily to defend its own fuel bill, and the cover frees Saudi aircraft for offensive sorties in British airframes — 72 Typhoons delivered, 48 more under negotiation.

global.headline: SUDAN'S ARMY DRONES KILL MOURNERS IN KORDOFAN AND BURN A FUEL MARKET IN ABYEI
summary: A drone hit a truck carrying about 200 mourners as it reached a funeral in al-Dabab, West Kordofan, on Sunday, killing 145, with five more in a second strike on the tent where mourners gathered, BBC sources said; the Tasis alliance puts the toll at 80. On Monday at 11am a strike on Amiet Market in Abyei ignited a fuel depot still burning on Tuesday. Abyei's caretaker information minister Yohanna Akol Ngor said "we have recorded 153 deaths" and the toll was rising as the fire burned; the BBC was given 73. Médecins Sans Frontières treated more than 20 wounded, several critical, at Ameth Bek Hospital.

A senior Sudanese officer said the army struck fuel tankers arriving from South Sudan for the Rapid Support Forces and that the dead were RSF members and smugglers: "We do not target civilians." South Sudan's foreign ministry blamed Sudan's military, summoned its ambassador and asked that Abyei be handled diplomatically.
global.geopolitical: Abyei's status was left open by the 2005 peace agreement and its referendum never held, so a strike there is both counter-smuggling and an attack on territory Juba claims — the clearest path from Sudan's civil war to a war between states.
global.socioeconomic: Interdicting fuel now means bombing where fuel is sold. Amiet is the hub shared by Ngok Dinka farmers and Misseriya herders, and the depot that burned supplied local businesses, not only the front.

global.headline: EBOLA REACHES NIGERIA, AND THE EPIDEMIC PASSES 9,000 CASES
summary: Nigeria confirmed its first case of the current Ebola epidemic on Tuesday: a woman in Abuja who had arrived from Uganda, developed symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a private hospital on 11 October. Health minister Muhammad Pate said 44 contacts had been identified and were being traced. The DRC-centred epidemic stood at 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths on 11 October — a crude fatality rate of 48.3 per cent, the deadliest Ebola outbreak on record. Kenya, which reported its first case on 6 October, has now confirmed eight.
global.geopolitical: The virus has crossed a border by aircraft twice in a fortnight and has now reached Africa's most populous country. Nigeria's disclosure within a day sets the standard the next government to find a case faces.
global.socioeconomic: Four days passed between admission and diagnosis in a capital-city private hospital. That interval decides how many of the 44 contacts become cases, and it is what surveillance funding buys back.

singapore.headline: THE ALUMNI PHASE OF PRIMARY ONE SHRINKS BY A FIFTH OR MORE AT THE MOST WANTED SCHOOLS
summary: From next year's Primary 1 exercise, schools with 180 or more vacancies must reserve 60 places for Phase 2C, open to every child, up from 40. Applying the Education Ministry's 2026 figures, CNA found that at 26 of the 35 schools oversubscribed in Phase 2A — the alumni phase — the extra Phase 2C places would come out of Phase 2A. Red Swastika School, the most oversubscribed this year with 88 applicants for 24 places, would be left with four. Princess Elizabeth Primary would go from 47 places for 137 applicants to 27; Shuqun and Pei Hwa Presbyterian also lose more than a quarter.

Twelve schools with enough Phase 2A places this year could become oversubscribed: Methodist Girls' School (Primary), 93 applicants for 95 places, would be left with 77. Separately, 12 schools in neighbourhoods where public housing is under 40 per cent of homes within 2km will split Phase 2C into two equal tracks, within and beyond 2km, with no distance priority inside either.
singapore.geopolitical: Each widening of Phase 2C is paid for out of an inherited claim. The alumni phase, created in 1999 to build school communities, is now the budget line funding open access — and it bites hardest at neighbourhood primaries, not the old names.
singapore.socioeconomic: Four places for 88 applicants turns a reasonable expectation into a lottery, and the 2km split removes distance as an advantage in exactly the districts where proximity was bought.

singapore.headline: SINGTEL FINED S$1 MILLION FOR THE MARCH OUTAGE THAT CUT 720,000 LINES OVER THREE DAYS
summary: IMDA fined Singtel S$1 million over mobile outages on 16, 18 and 19 March that hit 720,000 customers and disrupted online payments, ride-hailing and food delivery. A chiller system at a Singtel exchange broke down after a vendor failed to reopen a manual water valve following scheduled maintenance and Singtel did not actively monitor it, so network equipment overheated and shut down; when 5G traffic was redirected to a second exchange, a disabled packet optimiser and a software bug left it unable to carry the load. The incidents "were within Singtel's control to prevent" and were not a cyberattack, IMDA said, noting the S$8 million of goodwill rebates it had paid.

It is Singtel's second S$1 million penalty in ten months: IMDA fined it the same amount in December 2025 over an October 2024 fixed-voice failure that cut 500,000 users off from banks, hospitals and emergency lines for more than four hours. Singapore's largest telco, with about 4.5 million mobile subscribers, accepted the ruling; the biggest telecoms fine here remains S$6 million, in 2014.
singapore.geopolitical: A valve left shut by a contractor took down a tenth of the country's mobile base, and the fallback exchange had a disabled optimiser nobody had checked: the regulator is now fining maintenance governance, not outages.
singapore.socioeconomic: The penalty is an eighth of the rebates Singtel had already paid, a signal rather than a deterrent — and the services that failed, payments and delivery, have no non-digital fallback.

singapore.headline: A SIXTEENTH DAY OF UNHEALTHY AIR, THE N95 STOCKPILE OPENED, AND JAKARTA SAYS IT IS STILL CAPABLE
summary: Singapore is on its 16th day of unhealthy air, past the 14-day stretch of the 2015 crisis. The Health Ministry said on Tuesday it has released the national N95 stockpile to retailers: the masks are on sale at every FairPrice outlet and at Guardian, Unity and Watsons, with Cold Storage, Giant and Sheng Siong to follow this week. Grace Fu said FairPrice had just drawn from the stockpile and asked people to buy only what they need. Manpower told employers to work from hourly PM2.5 readings rather than only the next day's PSI forecast: elderly, pregnant and chronically ill workers should avoid outdoor work above 150 and be barred above 250, with N95s provided where strenuous outdoor work above 150 is unavoidable.

Indonesia has still not declared the fires a national disaster, the step that would oblige it to accept foreign help. "For now, we are still capable," coordinating minister Dudung Abdurachman said, citing fuel distribution constraints while adding that neighbours' help is welcome: Malaysia's three aircraft and 52 personnel may come, and Singapore's offer is routed through the national disaster agency. Jakarta has deployed 47 aircraft and 60,000 personnel, and its foreign minister said on 15 October that President Prabowo had approved foreign assistance.
singapore.geopolitical: Jakarta has approved help in principle and withheld the declaration that would let it arrive, so Singapore's firefighting and cloud-seeding offers sit with an agency rather than a government.
singapore.socioeconomic: Opening a national stockpile for haze rather than a pandemic, and writing hour-by-hour work rules, makes the smoke an occupational-health regime. The cost lands on construction, landscaping and delivery.

singapore.headline: SINGAPORE AND SWEDEN LINE UP HYDROGEN, AMMONIA AND GRID LESSONS FOR THE ASEAN POWER GRID
summary: Singapore and Sweden agreed on Tuesday, during President Tharman Shanmugaratnam's state visit, to explore hydrogen and ammonia, regional energy interconnectivity and high-voltage direct current technology together, the Energy Market Authority said. "Sweden's experience with cross-border energy management and regional grid integration is particularly relevant as South-east Asia develops the ASEAN Power Grid," Tharman said, having pointed at the state banquet to work already under way on ammonia-fuel-ready power generation. At the KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Tharman and King Carl XVI Gustaf watched KTH and the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy sign an agreement on training public sector leaders.
singapore.geopolitical: The ASEAN Power Grid needs someone who has run power across borders between governments that disagree, which is what Sweden sells — and it is the quietest route by which European nuclear experience reaches a Singapore studying small modular reactors.
singapore.socioeconomic: Interconnection and HVDC are how imported low-carbon electricity would physically arrive. Hydrogen and ammonia remain the expensive half, which is why this week's deliverable was a study visit.

word.definition: A province ruled by a governor on behalf of a distant sovereign; by extension, a territory that is nominally its own but whose decisions are taken elsewhere.
word.etymology: From Old Persian khshathrapavan, protector of the realm, the title borne by provincial governors of the Achaemenid empire, through Greek satrapes and Latin satrapia into English in the fourteenth century.
word.example: Kallas's charge that American negotiators have spent a year and a half pushing Kyiv towards surrender, and Zelensky's refusal of a Trump-Putin-Xi summit held without him, are objections to the same thing: being treated as a satrapy rather than a state.
